verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.help: Our overall conclusion for the environment, combining all the checks below.

works.label: Works
works.short: Installs, loads and runs, and produces scores.
works.long: The environment passed our run test. If it also has a 'Scores correct answers higher' result, check that too: running fine doesn't by itself prove the score measures the right thing.

works_weak_reward.label: Works, weak scoring
works_weak_reward.short: It runs, but its score only loosely tracks whether the answer is right.
works_weak_reward.long: Review found that the reward gives credit for things other than correctness (for example format or length), so a model can score well without being right. Numbers from it should be read with care.
works_weak_reward.action: Author: make the reward depend on the answer being correct. User: don't rely on its scores as an accuracy measure.

undeclared_deps.label: Missing dependency
undeclared_deps.short: Works only after installing a package the environment uses but forgot to list.
undeclared_deps.long: A normal install crashes on first use because a required package isn't in the environment's dependency list. Once that package is added, it works. Easy fix for the author.
undeclared_deps.action: Author: add the missing package to pyproject.toml dependencies. User: install it manually first.

works_undeclared_deps.label: Missing dependency
works_undeclared_deps.short: Works only after installing a package the environment uses but forgot to list.
works_undeclared_deps.long: A normal install crashes on first use because a required package isn't in the environment's dependency list. Once that package is added, it works. Easy fix for the author.
works_undeclared_deps.action: Author: add the missing package to pyproject.toml dependencies. User: install it manually first.

rotted.label: Broken by updates
rotted.short: Broken today, but it worked with the package versions from the day it was published.
rotted.long: Nothing was wrong with the environment when it came out; a newer release of a package it relies on (usually the verifiers library) changed and broke it. It can usually be revived by pinning the old versions.
rotted.action: Author: update the code for the new version, or pin the versions that worked. User: install with the older versions pinned.

broken.label: Broken
broken.short: It fails today and also failed with the package versions from its publish date.
broken.long: This is a real defect in the environment itself, not something caused by later updates. See the 'Failed at' reason for what went wrong.
broken.action: Author: fix the error shown. User: avoid it until fixed.

hollow.label: Fake scoring or data
hollow.short: It runs without errors, but its score or its tasks are fake, so its numbers are meaningless.
hollow.long: Examples: the reward is always the same number, the dataset is a placeholder, or the code silently swaps in dummy data when the real data fails to load. This is the worst kind of problem because nothing looks wrong: you get scores, they just don't mean anything.
hollow.action: Author: use the real data and a reward that checks correctness, and let load errors surface. User: don't use its results.

not_installable.label: Not installable
not_installable.short: The hub has no installable build of this version.
not_installable.long: The hub lists this environment, but there is no built package for the listed version, so a normal install cannot get it.
not_installable.action: Author: re-publish so the hub builds the package.

unverifiable_here.label: Can't verify here
unverifiable_here.short: It needs something we didn't provide, so we can't say whether it works.
unverifiable_here.long: Typical needs: Prime's paid sandboxes or login, API keys for outside services, Docker, a GPU, an AI judge model, or required settings that its README documents. Unknown is not the same as broken.
unverifiable_here.action: Test it yourself with what it needs.

listed_but_missing.label: Listed but missing
listed_but_missing.short: It's in the hub listing, but its page or package is gone.
listed_but_missing.long: We couldn't download it at all. It was most likely deleted or made private after it was listed.
listed_but_missing.action: Users: pick another environment. Hub: remove stale listings.

harness.label: Our test failed
harness.short: Our testing setup failed, so we have no verdict on this environment.
harness.long: Something in our own test machinery went wrong (not the environment). Treat it as untested.

status.title: Run test result
status.help: What happened when we installed it like a user and ran 5 tasks twice with a fake model.

pass.label: Ran fine
pass.short: It installed, loaded and ran its tasks, and produced a score.
pass.long: Every step of our test went through: the package installed like a normal user would install it, the environment loaded its tasks, and our fake model got scored. This says nothing yet about whether the score is meaningful; that is what the scoring check is for.

pass_with_fixes.label: Ran after a fix
pass_with_fixes.short: It only ran after we installed a package the environment uses but forgot to list.
pass_with_fixes.long: A normal install crashes because a required package is missing from the environment's dependency list. Once we added that package by hand, everything ran. Easy fix for the author.
pass_with_fixes.action: Author: add the missing package to the dependencies in pyproject.toml. User: install that package yourself before using the environment.

fail.label: Failed
fail.short: Something went wrong while installing, loading or running it.
fail.long: The environment crashed or errored at some step. The 'Failed at' column says which step and why. Failures were confirmed as real for a sample of environments by a separate review.
fail.action: Check the error and the 'Failed at' reason for the specific fix.

blocked.label: Can't verify here
blocked.short: It needs something we deliberately didn't provide, such as paid credentials, API keys, Docker or a GPU.
blocked.long: We stopped at a point where the environment asked for an outside resource, so we don't know whether it works. This is not a sign it is broken.
blocked.action: Test it yourself with the required credentials or hardware.

harness.label: Our test failed
harness.short: Our own testing setup had a problem, so there is no result for this environment.
harness.long: The failure came from our test machinery (for example a virtual machine that didn't start), not from the environment. Treat it as untested.

unlisted_404.label: Listed but missing
unlisted_404.short: The hub lists it, but its page or package can no longer be downloaded.
unlisted_404.long: It appears in the hub's listing, but when we tried to fetch it the hub returned 'not found'. Most likely it was deleted or made private after being listed.
unlisted_404.action: Users: pick another environment. Hub: remove stale listings.

not_run.label: Not tested
not_run.short: We didn't run this test for this environment.
not_run.long: This step was skipped, usually because an earlier step already failed or the test didn't apply.

asof_status.title: Result with original versions
asof_status.help: The same run test, repeated with the package versions from the day the environment was published. Tells 'always broken' apart from 'broken by later updates'.

pass.label: Ran fine
pass.short: It installed, loaded and ran its tasks, and produced a score.
pass.long: Every step of our test went through: the package installed like a normal user would install it, the environment loaded its tasks, and our fake model got scored. This says nothing yet about whether the score is meaningful; that is what the scoring check is for.

pass_with_fixes.label: Ran after a fix
pass_with_fixes.short: It only ran after we installed a package the environment uses but forgot to list.
pass_with_fixes.long: A normal install crashes because a required package is missing from the environment's dependency list. Once we added that package by hand, everything ran. Easy fix for the author.
pass_with_fixes.action: Author: add the missing package to the dependencies in pyproject.toml. User: install that package yourself before using the environment.

fail.label: Failed
fail.short: Something went wrong while installing, loading or running it.
fail.long: The environment crashed or errored at some step. The 'Failed at' column says which step and why. Failures were confirmed as real for a sample of environments by a separate review.
fail.action: Check the error and the 'Failed at' reason for the specific fix.

blocked.label: Can't verify here
blocked.short: It needs something we deliberately didn't provide, such as paid credentials, API keys, Docker or a GPU.
blocked.long: We stopped at a point where the environment asked for an outside resource, so we don't know whether it works. This is not a sign it is broken.
blocked.action: Test it yourself with the required credentials or hardware.

harness.label: Our test failed
harness.short: Our own testing setup had a problem, so there is no result for this environment.
harness.long: The failure came from our test machinery (for example a virtual machine that didn't start), not from the environment. Treat it as untested.

unlisted_404.label: Listed but missing
unlisted_404.short: The hub lists it, but its page or package can no longer be downloaded.
unlisted_404.long: It appears in the hub's listing, but when we tried to fetch it the hub returned 'not found'. Most likely it was deleted or made private after being listed.
unlisted_404.action: Users: pick another environment. Hub: remove stale listings.

not_run.label: Not tested
not_run.short: We didn't run this test for this environment.
not_run.long: This step was skipped, usually because an earlier step already failed or the test didn't apply.

scaling.title: Scores correct answers higher?
scaling.help: We compared the score for the environment's own correct answers against the score for nonsense. A useful environment scores correct answers clearly higher.

scales.label: Scoring makes sense
scales.short: Correct answers clearly score higher than nonsense.
scales.long: When our fake model gave the environment's own reference answers, the score was clearly higher than when it gave nonsense. That's the minimum you'd expect from a working scorer.

weak.label: Barely tells apart
weak.short: Correct answers score only a little higher than nonsense.
weak.long: The scorer reacts to correctness, but not by much. Often this is because the reward also counts format or other things, or because our correct answer wasn't in exactly the format it wants. Flagged cases were reviewed; see the review reason.
weak.action: Check the review reason before trusting its scores.

flat.label: Can't tell apart
flat.short: Correct answers and nonsense get about the same score.
flat.long: That's suspicious: a scorer that can't tell right from wrong is useless for training. But often the cause is on our side (wrong answer format) or the test doesn't apply (for example, the score comes from an AI judge). Flagged cases were reviewed; see the review reason.
flat.action: Check the review reason; only reasons marked as a real problem count against the environment.

inverted.label: Nonsense scores higher
inverted.short: Our nonsense answer scored higher than the correct answer.
inverted.long: That's backwards and suspicious. It can mean a scoring bug, or that our correct answer didn't reach the environment in the form it expects. Flagged cases were reviewed; see the review reason.

no_gold_hits.label: Test didn't land
no_gold_hits.short: Our correct answers never reached the environment's scorer, so this test is inconclusive.
no_gold_hits.long: We couldn't match our reference answers to the tasks being asked (for example, the environment shuffles or rewrites its tasks), so we have no comparison.

no_answers.label: No answers to test
no_answers.short: The environment has no reference answers, so this test can't be done.
no_answers.long: Many environments grade with tests, rules or a judge instead of a stored answer. That's normal; it just means this particular check doesn't apply.

not_run.label: Not tested
not_run.short: We didn't run the scoring check for this environment.
not_run.long: The scoring check only runs on environments that passed the run test, and a few were skipped.

gold_best_fmt.title: Answer format that worked
gold_best_fmt.help: How we had to write the correct answer for the environment's scorer to accept it best.

raw.label: Plain answer
raw.short: The scorer accepted the reference answer as-is.
raw.long: We sent the correct answer exactly as stored, with no wrapping, and that scored best.

boxed.label: Boxed answer
boxed.short: The scorer wanted the answer written as \boxed{answer}.
boxed.long: This math-style wrapping is a common convention; the environment's scorer looks for the answer inside it.

xml.label: Tagged answer
xml.short: The scorer wanted the answer inside <answer>...</answer> tags.
xml.long: Many environments ask the model to put its final answer in tags so it can be found reliably.

parser.label: Env's own format
parser.short: The scorer wanted the answer wrapped in the environment's own custom tag.
parser.long: We read which tag the environment's answer-reader expects and wrapped the correct answer in it.

custom.label: Reviewer's format
custom.short: A reviewer worked out the exact answer format this environment expects.
custom.long: Our automatic formats didn't fit, so a reviewer looked at the code and wrote the answer the way the scorer needs it, then we re-ran the check.

gold_review_cause.title: Why the scoring looked off
gold_review_cause.help: For environments where correct answers didn't clearly beat nonsense, a reviewer found the reason. Only 'Scoring bug' and 'Score ignores correctness' are real problems with the environment.

harness_format.label: Our format was wrong
harness_format.short: The environment is fine; our correct answer wasn't in the format it expects.
harness_format.long: The low score was our test's fault: the scorer needed the answer written a specific way and our reference answer didn't match. Not a problem with the environment.

harness_pairing.label: Answer sent to wrong task
harness_pairing.short: Our correct answer was matched to the wrong question.
harness_pairing.long: Our test sent a reference answer to a different task than the one it belongs to, so a low score is expected. Not a problem with the environment.

answer_not_target.label: Test doesn't apply
answer_not_target.short: The environment's stored 'answer' isn't something a model would reply with.
answer_not_target.long: In these environments the answer field holds an id, a spec or test data, not the reply a model should give, so sending it back as a reply isn't a fair test. Not a problem with the environment.

judge_or_external.label: Needs a judge
judge_or_external.short: The score comes from an AI judge or an outside service we didn't have.
judge_or_external.long: Without the judge or service the scorer can't do its job in our test, so the comparison tells us nothing. Unknown, not broken.
judge_or_external.action: Test it with the judge or service configured.

grader_bug.label: Scoring bug
grader_bug.short: Real problem: a correct answer still scores low because of a bug in the scoring code.
grader_bug.long: Reviewers confirmed the environment's scorer mishandles right answers (for example, compares the wrong fields or parses them incorrectly). Training on it would teach a model the wrong thing.
grader_bug.action: Author: fix the scoring code. User: don't trust its scores until fixed.

reward_not_correctness.label: Score ignores correctness
reward_not_correctness.short: Real problem: the score doesn't depend on whether the answer is right.
reward_not_correctness.long: Reviewers confirmed the reward measures something else (format, length, effort) rather than correctness, so a model can score well while being wrong.
reward_not_correctness.action: Author: make the reward check correctness. User: don't use its scores as an accuracy measure.

unclear.label: Unclear
unclear.long: The evidence wasn't enough to say whether the problem is in the environment or in our test.

gold_review_genuine.title: Real scoring problem?
gold_review_genuine.help: Whether the scoring review found a genuine problem in the environment (as opposed to a limit of our test).

true.label: Real problem
true.short: At least one review found a real scoring problem in the environment.
true.long: The scoring check's suspicious result was confirmed as the environment's fault (scoring bug or score ignoring correctness).
true.action: Author: fix the scoring. User: don't trust its scores.

false.label: Not the env's fault
false.short: Reviews found the suspicious scoring result was not the environment's fault.
false.long: The cause was our test (format, pairing), a check that doesn't apply, or a judge we didn't have.

audit_verdict.title: Review finding
audit_verdict.help: For a sample of failures and suspicious environments, a human or AI reviewer read the code and logs to check our automatic result. Several findings can be combined with '+'.

genuine.label: Confirmed real
genuine.short: A reviewer confirmed the failure is a real problem in the environment.
genuine.long: Someone (human or AI) read the code and logs and found the actual cause in the environment, not in our setup.

artifact.label: Our setup's fault
artifact.short: A reviewer found the failure was caused by our testing setup, not the environment.
artifact.long: The environment may well work; our test environment tripped it up. Treat the automatic result for this one as wrong.

unclear.label: Unclear
unclear.short: A reviewer couldn't tell whether the failure is real.
unclear.long: The code and logs didn't give enough evidence either way.

hollow.label: Fake scoring or data
hollow.short: A reviewer confirmed the score or data is fake.
hollow.long: Confirmed: the reward is constant, the data is a placeholder, or real data is silently replaced with dummy data. Its numbers are meaningless.

weak.label: Weak scoring
weak.short: A reviewer found the score only loosely tracks correctness.
weak.long: It works, but a model can score well without being right.

benign.label: False alarm
benign.short: Our automatic scan flagged it, but a reviewer found nothing wrong.
benign.long: The code pattern the scanner looks for was there, but it is harmless in this case.

hollow_flags.title: Fake-scoring warning signs
hollow_flags.help: Patterns our automatic code scan flagged as possible signs of fake scoring or data. A flag is a reason to look closer, not proof; reviews decide.

swallowed_dataset.label: Hides data errors
swallowed_dataset.short: If loading the real data fails, the code silently carries on, possibly with fallback or empty data.
swallowed_dataset.long: Our code scan found error handling that catches a failed dataset load without stopping. If that happens you get scores on the wrong data with no warning. Some of these are harmless; reviews decide.

dummy_rows.label: Placeholder data
dummy_rows.short: The code contains placeholder or toy tasks instead of (or alongside) real data.
dummy_rows.long: Our code scan found hardcoded sample tasks such as 'Reply with OK.'. If those are what actually gets used, scores are meaningless. Reviews decide.
dummy_rows.action: Author: replace placeholders with the real dataset.

const_reward.label: Constant score
const_reward.short: A scoring function gives the same score no matter what the answer is.
const_reward.long: Our code scan found a reward that always returns the same number (for example always 1.0 for any non-empty answer). A score that never changes can't tell good from bad.
const_reward.action: Author: make the reward depend on the answer.

scanner_gaming.label: Mentions quality scan
scanner_gaming.short: The code refers to the hub's quality scan, which may mean it was written to pass the scan rather than to be useful.
scanner_gaming.long: Our scan noticed text referring to the hub's quality check inside the environment's code. That can be harmless, but it can also signal an environment built to look good to automated checks. Reviews decide.

runtime.title: Library version
runtime.help: Which generation of the verifiers library the environment is built on.

VERIFIERS_V0.label: Older format
VERIFIERS_V0.short: Built on the older version of the verifiers library.
VERIFIERS_V0.long: Most environments use this original format. Newer releases of the library have changed some of it, which is a common source of breakage.

VERIFIERS_V1.label: Newer format
VERIFIERS_V1.short: Built on the newer, task-set version of the verifiers library.
VERIFIERS_V1.long: A newer way to package environments. Some of these need newer command-line tools to run.

official.title: Publisher
official.help: Whether the environment comes from Prime Intellect itself or from the community.

true.label: Official
true.short: Published by Prime Intellect itself (primeintellect, prime-community or prime).
true.long: Maintained by the hub's operator rather than a community member.

false.label: Community
false.long: Anyone can publish to the hub, so quality varies widely.

install.label: Installing
install.short: Installing the package and the packages it depends on, like a user would.

load.label: Setting up tasks
load.short: Building the environment and loading its dataset of tasks.

rollout.label: Running tasks
rollout.short: Actually running tasks with the fake model and scoring the answers.

harness.label: Our test setup
harness.short: A step in our own testing machinery, not the environment.

ok.label: No problem
ok.long: No failure was recorded at any step.

undeclared_dependency.label: Unlisted package
undeclared_dependency.short: It uses a package that isn't in its dependency list; it ran once we installed it.
undeclared_dependency.long: A normal install crashes on first use. Adding the missing package fixes it.
undeclared_dependency.action: Author: add the package to pyproject.toml dependencies.

resolver_conflict.label: Conflicting requirements
resolver_conflict.short: The packages it needs ask for versions that can't all be installed together.
resolver_conflict.long: The installer can't find a combination of versions that satisfies every requirement, so nothing gets installed. Often caused by pinning an old or exact version of a shared library.
resolver_conflict.action: Author: loosen or update the version requirements.

build_failure.label: Package won't build
build_failure.short: A package it depends on fails to compile during install.
build_failure.long: Some packages have to be compiled on install; this one failed, often because it needs system tools or doesn't support the Python version.
build_failure.action: Author: pick a dependency with ready-made builds, or document the system requirements.

package_missing.label: Package not available
package_missing.short: The package isn't available to download.
package_missing.long: The install couldn't find the environment's package or one of its dependencies.
package_missing.action: Author: publish the package (or fix the name).

version_not_on_hub.label: Version not available
version_not_on_hub.short: The listed version can't be downloaded from the hub.
version_not_on_hub.long: The hub lists a version that it doesn't actually serve, so installing it fails.
version_not_on_hub.action: Author: republish the version. Hub: fix the listing.

python_version.label: Wrong Python version
python_version.short: It doesn't support the Python version we used.
python_version.long: The package declares (or needs) a Python version different from the standard one we tested with.
python_version.action: Author: support current Python versions or document the requirement.

verifiers_api_drift.label: Library changed
verifiers_api_drift.short: The code uses part of the verifiers library that was changed or removed in a newer release.
verifiers_api_drift.long: The environment was written against an older version of the library it's built on. If it worked with its publish-day versions it is 'Broken by updates', otherwise 'Broken'.
verifiers_api_drift.action: Author: update the code to the current library, or pin the version that worked.

missing_dependency.label: Unlisted package
missing_dependency.short: The code uses a package that it doesn't list as a requirement.
missing_dependency.long: Installing it the normal way leaves that package out, so it crashes on first use.
missing_dependency.action: Author: add the package to pyproject.toml dependencies.

relative_import.label: Packaging mistake
relative_import.short: The code imports its own files in a way that only works on the author's machine.
relative_import.long: Imports that rely on the current folder break once the code is installed as a package.

invalid_taskset_export.label: Packaging mistake
invalid_taskset_export.short: The package doesn't expose its tasks the way the newer library format expects.
invalid_taskset_export.long: The newer verifiers format needs the environment to export its task set in a specific way; this one doesn't, so it can't be loaded.
invalid_taskset_export.action: Author: export the task set as the library documents.

no_load_environment.label: Missing entry point
no_load_environment.short: The package has no load_environment function, the standard way to start an environment.
no_load_environment.long: Tools look for that function to create the environment; without it nothing can use the package.

template_stub.label: Unedited template
template_stub.short: The author published the unchanged starter template, with no real environment inside.
template_stub.long: The package is the empty example that comes with the project generator, so there is nothing to run.
template_stub.action: Author: finish the environment or unpublish it.

dataset_load.label: Dataset unavailable
dataset_load.short: Its dataset is missing, private, gated or not shipped with the package.
dataset_load.long: The tasks can't be loaded, so nothing can run. Common causes: a private or gated Hugging Face dataset, or data files that weren't included in the package.
dataset_load.action: Author: make the dataset public or include the files in the package.

hardcoded_path.label: Reads author's files
hardcoded_path.short: It reads a file from a location that only exists on the author's own computer.
hardcoded_path.long: The code points at a fixed path like /home/someone/data, which doesn't exist anywhere else.
hardcoded_path.action: Author: ship the file with the package and find it relative to the code.

requires_env_args.label: Needs settings
requires_env_args.short: It needs settings that its README documents but that we didn't provide.
requires_env_args.long: The environment won't start without specific arguments (such as a data path or mode). We don't count this as broken.
requires_env_args.action: User: pass the settings the README describes.

needs_prime_auth.label: Needs Prime login
needs_prime_auth.short: It needs a Prime Intellect account login we didn't provide.
needs_prime_auth.long: Some environments use Prime's own services and require signing in. We can't verify these here; unknown, not broken.
needs_prime_auth.action: Test it while logged in to Prime.

needs_sandbox_runtime.label: Needs Prime sandbox
needs_sandbox_runtime.short: It runs code inside Prime's paid sandboxes, which we didn't provide.
needs_sandbox_runtime.long: Code-execution environments often send the model's code to remote sandboxes. Unknown, not broken.
needs_sandbox_runtime.action: Test it with Prime sandbox access.

needs_credentials.label: Needs API key
needs_credentials.short: It needs an API key or credentials for an outside service.
needs_credentials.long: For example a key for a search API or another model provider. Unknown, not broken.
needs_credentials.action: Test it with the required keys set.

needs_docker.label: Needs Docker
needs_docker.short: It needs Docker (a container tool) to run, which we didn't provide.
needs_docker.long: Some environments launch containers for each task. Unknown, not broken.
needs_docker.action: Test it on a machine with Docker.

mock_loop.label: Needs a real model
mock_loop.short: A multi-step game or conversation our fake model can't play, so it ran until the time limit.
mock_loop.long: Our fake model always gives the same reply, so the environment kept waiting for a valid move. This doesn't mean it's broken; it needs a real model.
mock_loop.action: Test it with a real model.

timeout.label: Took too long
timeout.short: It didn't finish within our time limit.
timeout.long: It may be very slow (for example downloading a huge dataset) or stuck.
timeout.action: Author: check startup time and large downloads.

oom.label: Ran out of memory
oom.short: It used more memory than our test machine had.
oom.long: Often caused by loading a very large dataset or model into memory up front.
oom.action: Author: load data lazily or document memory needs.

network.label: Network error
network.short: A download or connection failed during the test.
network.long: It may be a temporary outage or a link that no longer works.
network.action: Check whether the URL it uses still works.

exception.label: Crashed
exception.short: It crashed with an error not covered by the other reasons.
exception.long: See the error message for details.

no_rewards_written.label: No score produced
no_rewards_written.short: It ran but never produced any scores.
no_rewards_written.long: The run finished without recording a reward, so there's nothing to evaluate.
no_rewards_written.action: Author: check that the reward function runs and returns a number.

pypi_cache.label: Test setup: package cache
pypi_cache.short: Our test setup's local package cache failed.
pypi_cache.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

dist_name_lookup.label: Test setup: name lookup
dist_name_lookup.short: Our test setup couldn't work out the package's install name.
dist_name_lookup.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

readonly_cwd.label: Test setup: read-only folder
readonly_cwd.short: The environment tried to write to a folder our test machine kept read-only.
readonly_cwd.long: Counted as a problem with our setup rather than the environment. Treat as untested.

no_v1_cli.label: Test setup: missing tool
no_v1_cli.short: Our test setup lacked the newer command-line tool these environments need.
no_v1_cli.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

v1_on_legacy_path.label: Test setup: wrong runner
v1_on_legacy_path.short: We ran a newer-format environment with the older-format runner.
v1_on_legacy_path.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

vm_failure.label: Test setup: VM failed
vm_failure.short: The throwaway virtual machine running the test failed.
vm_failure.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

agent_error.label: Test setup: agent error
agent_error.short: The program inside our test machine that drives the test crashed.
agent_error.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

corrupt_result.label: Test setup: bad result
corrupt_result.short: The test's result file came back damaged.
corrupt_result.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

incomplete.label: Test setup: unfinished
incomplete.short: The test didn't finish, so there's no result.
incomplete.long: A problem in our testing machinery, not the environment. Treat as untested.

concepts.plain: A small package that defines a task for an AI model: a set of questions or tasks plus a scoring rule. People use them to test models (evals) or to train them with reinforcement learning.
Prime Intellect's public catalog of about 1,800 environments, where anyone can publish one and anyone can install it with `prime env install`.
The score an environment gives a model's answer, usually between 0 and 1. Training pushes the model toward higher reward, so a reward that doesn't track correctness teaches the wrong thing.
The open-source Python library almost every environment is built on. It changes over time, and older environments can break when it does.
One attempt at one task: the model answers and the environment scores it. We ran 5 tasks x 2 attempts per environment.
A stand-in for a real AI model that gives scripted replies. It lets us test thousands of environments cheaply, but it can't play games or hold real conversations.
Gold is the environment's own reference answer; garbage is a fixed nonsense reply ('I think the answer is 0'). A healthy environment scores gold clearly higher.
A throwaway virtual machine we created for each test, so each environment was installed from scratch in isolation and then thrown away.
Dependencies are the other packages an environment needs. Pinning means fixing them to specific versions, which keeps an environment working when those packages later change.
One that runs without errors but whose scores or data are fake, so its results are meaningless even though nothing looks wrong.

how_it_works.plain: We listed every environment on the hub (about 1,835) and downloaded its source code.

In a fresh throwaway machine per environment, we installed it like a normal user, loaded it, and ran 5 tasks twice with a fake model that always answers the same nonsense. A working environment must install, load and produce a score.
We ran it again with the fake model giving the environment's own correct answers. Correct answers should score clearly higher than nonsense.
For failures, we reinstalled with the package versions from the day the environment was published, to separate 'always broken' from 'broken later by updates'.
An automatic code scan flagged signs of fake rewards or placeholder data, and reviewers checked the flagged ones.
Human and AI reviewers read the code and logs for a sample of failures and suspicious scores to confirm they are real and not caused by our setup.

caveats: We used a fake model with scripted replies, not a real AI model. Passing means the environment runs and scores answers; it does not mean it's a good benchmark or training task.
'Can't verify here' is not 'broken'. Those environments needed credentials, paid sandboxes, API keys, Docker, a GPU or an AI judge that we deliberately didn't provide.
Results reflect package versions as of the test date. An environment that works today can break with the next library release, and a broken one may be fixed after we tested.
We ran only 5 tasks x 2 attempts per environment, so problems that show up only on rare tasks or long runs can be missed.
Human/AI review covered a sample of failures and suspicious cases, not every environment. Unreviewed results are automatic and can occasionally be wrong.
The fake-scoring scan looks for known patterns. It can raise false alarms (reviews mark these 'False alarm') and can miss fake scoring written in other ways.
The 'scores correct answers higher' check needs stored reference answers. Environments graded by tests, rules or an AI judge can't be checked this way.
